title: Azure (AKS) & Google Cloud (GKE) Multi-Cloud Architecture
summary: Operate multi-cloud Kubernetes fleets across Microsoft Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE Autopilot/Standard) with federated workload identity.
learningObjectives: Provision and inspect Azure AKS and Google GKE clusters using `az aks` and `gcloud container` CLIs.
Configure Azure Entra Workload Identity and GKE Workload Identity Federation on ServiceAccounts.

curriculumModules.title: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) & Entra Workload Identity
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: AKS integrates Azure CNI Overlay, Cilium dataplanes, and Microsoft Entra Workload Identity using OIDC token federation (`azure.workload.identity/client-id`).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy AKS across 3 Availability Zones with Entra Workload Identity and Azure Key Vault CSI Secret Store Provider.

curriculumModules.title: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE Autopilot) & Fleet Federation
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: GKE Autopilot manages node provisioning, security hardening, and bin-packing automatically while GKE Workload Identity binds Kubernetes ServiceAccounts to Google IAM Service Accounts.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use Multi-Cluster Ingress / Gateway API and Workload Identity (`iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account`) for zero-key multi-region GKE fleets.

labs.title: Provisioning & Auditing Azure AKS and Google GKE Clusters
labs.scenario: Verify multi-cloud control plane readiness across Azure AKS (`kubelabs-aks-prod`) and Google GKE (`kubelabs-gke-autopilot`) using `az` and `gcloud` CLIs.
labs.productionContext: Enterprise platform engineers manage multi-cloud Kubernetes control planes across AWS, Azure, and GCP to meet regulatory and availability mandates.
objectives: Inspect Azure AKS cluster `kubelabs-aks-prod` using `az aks show --name kubelabs-aks-prod`
Inspect Google GKE cluster `kubelabs-gke-autopilot` using `gcloud container clusters describe kubelabs-gke-autopilot`
labs.starterManifest:
# Multi-Cloud Fleet Target Inventory
clusters:
  - provider: azure
    name: kubelabs-aks-prod
  - provider: gcp
    name: kubelabs-gke-autopilot

steps.title: Audit Google GKE Autopilot Control Plane

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure both `az aks` and `gcloud container` commands have been executed.

labs.title: Configuring GKE & Azure Federated Workload Identity
labs.scenario: Create a federated `ServiceAccount` (`multicloud-identity-sa`) in `production` annotated with `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account=telemetry@kubelabs-gcp.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
labs.productionContext: Workload Identity Federation allows Kubernetes pods to authenticate to Google Cloud and Azure APIs without downloading JSON service account keys.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: multicloud-identity-sa
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: telemetry@kubelabs-gcp.iam.gserviceaccount.com

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary operational benefit of Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot mode compared to Standard mode?
options: Google fully manages worker node provisioning, security hardening, and bin-packing, billing only for running Pod resource requests
It allows SSH root login to Google's physical routers
assessmentQuestions.explanation: GKE Autopilot manages the entire node infrastructure lifecycle and security posture automatically based on Pod specifications.

assessmentQuestions.question: Across AWS (IRSA), Azure (Entra Workload Identity), and GCP (Workload Identity Federation), what standard protocol underpins keyless Pod-to-Cloud IAM authentication?
options: Static IAM access keys committed to Git
assessmentQuestions.explanation: All three major cloud providers use OIDC federation to trust short-lived JWT tokens issued by the Kubernetes API server.
